issue.title: palace(status) tool call fails: 'int' object is not iterable
issue.symptom: 2026-11-17 web_vdaj_test6, turn 'where were we before that?': Core called palace(action=status, {}); gaia-core logged 'Tool call execution failed: 'int' object is not iterable' and she replied 'That didn't work on my end'. Find where the palace status result is iterated (main.py inline tool path, tool_result_text?).

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-common/tests/test_tool_call_parser_415r.py
"""Tests for gaia_common.utils.tool_call_parser.ToolCallParser.

No test file existed for this module before GAIA_Project-415r, so this
covers both the new <tool_calling: domain.action> variant (the actual bug
fix) and baseline regression coverage for the pre-existing <tool_call> JSON
and meta-verb formats, which had zero automated coverage.

Context (415r): live 2026-08-15, Prime emitted
'<tool_calling: knowledge.search> {"query": "King Arthur"} </tool_calling>'
— a 4th tag format (domain.action embedded IN the open tag, bare params
JSON body) that ToolCallParser didn't recognize at all, so it leaked to the
user as raw text instead of executing. Same failure class as GAIA_Project-pfdw.
"""

from gaia_common.utils.tool_call_parser import (
    ToolCallParser,
    ParseEventType,
)


def test_palace_status_counts_are_not_works():
    """sk6m: palace(status) has "works": 13 (a count); the turn died with
    "'int' object is not iterable"."""
    from gaia_common.utils.tool_call_parser import tool_result_text
    text = tool_result_text({"ok": True, "total_memories": 115, "works": 13,
                             "lookups": {"active": 2078}}, question="where were we?")
    assert "115" in text
